summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen and Tom Kelly watched Jim Corbett at Havlin's Theater and judged him fit, with Allen calling him the fastest big man he ever saw and predicting he would beat Fitzsimmons.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Friday, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, January 22, 1897. The theater visit was the Thursday matinee, Jan. 21.

facts.fact: Allen ran a saloon and concert hall on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh streets, St. Louis, and presided over the concert hall every night
places: Market Street between Sixth and Seventh streets, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen and Tom Kelly inspected Jim Corbett from a box at a Havlin's Theater matinee at the Post-Dispatch's request and declared him fit to fight
Allen had seen Corbett beat Kilrain, Mitchell and Sullivan, and lost money betting against him in the Sullivan fight
facts.quote: I lost money on him in the Sullivan fight, because I misjudged him, thinking him too light and spare.

facts.fact: Allen judged Corbett the fastest big man he had seen
facts.quote: He is the fastest and quickest big man I ever saw in my life, bar none.

facts.fact: Allen said he had fought at 145 pounds
facts.quote: He don't measure about the chest by eight inches what I did when I fought at 145 pounds, but he is a taller man than I was then.
